subject: POC capacity planning - Acme AI
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-15T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: POC capacity planning - Acme AI

Hi Alex / Team,

Thanks again for the call today — great to learn more about the Acme AI evaluation goals. Per our discussion, I captured a short recap, the proposed success criteria, and next steps so we can align on scope and timing for the POC:

1) High-level goal
- Validate Redwood inference for Acme's multi-tenant chat assistant (16k context) with SLA targets and predictable unit economics.

2) Success criteria (what you told us you care about)
- Latency: p95 generation latency < 300ms for typical 512-token prompts (target < 200ms for single-turn flows)
- Throughput: sustain 50 concurrent requests with spikes to 150 req/s for short bursts
- Cost: per-token unit cost within your benchmarked target (we'll provide estimated costs by model/quant profile)
- Quality: parity with your baseline model on the provided eval set (we'll run the eval harness)

3) Proposed POC scope and timeline
- Duration: 2 weeks (pilot), with option to extend 1 week for stress testing
- Start date: target week of Mar 8 (flexible if you need earlier)
- Deliverables: deployment in Dedicated POC environment, perf report, cost breakdown, and recommended runbook for production rollout

4) Capacity & infra (initial suggestion)
- Reserved baseline: 4 x H100-equivalent GPUs (to meet latency & throughput targets for your 16k sequences)
- Autoscaling policy: scale to 8 GPUs for sustained spikes > 100 req/s or queue depth > 75% for 2+ minutes; burst mode to 12 GPUs for short bursts (under our burst budget)
- Fallback strategy: automatic model-variant routing (smaller quantized model) if capacity is constrained

5) Ownership
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (AE) — commercial/coordination; Monica Patel (SE) — POC engineering/benchmarks; Dylan Brooks (CS) — post-POC onboarding/optimization
- Acme: Alex Johnson — technical owner; please let us know if there are other internal owners to loop in.

6) Next steps (action items)
- Alex: confirm acceptance criteria above + preferred POC start window (reply)
- Marissa/Monica: share SOW + capacity estimate (attached) and schedule kick-off call once dates confirmed
- Dylan: prepare playbook for handoff to production if POC meets criteria

Attachments: POC_SOW_AcmeAI_v1.pdf, capacity_sheet_acme.xlsx (attached)

Thanks — I can jump on a 30-min kick-off as soon as you confirm dates.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme-ai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-16T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC capacity planning - Acme AI

Thanks Marissa — nice summary and aligned on most items. A few clarifications and requests from our side: 

- Success criteria: agree on p95 < 300ms as a hard stop; we'd like to aim for < 200ms for the 90th percentile. For quality, we'll share a 500-prompt eval set by EOD Monday.

- Capacity ask: our traffic profile is slightly burstier than we described on the call. We expect baseline steady-state of ~40 req/s but with multiple product-driven bursts up to 180-200 req/s that can last 2–5 minutes. For trial purposes we want to avoid dropped requests; can you confirm your autoscaling from 4 -> 8 GPUs will handle those bursts? If not, we may need to reserve additional burst capacity (e.g., 2 hot spare GPUs) or accept a brief degradation during peak.

- Data/control plane: we need to validate data retention and audit logs during the POC. Please include a SOC2 evidence checklist or relevant docs.

- Timing: Mar 8 works best for us but we can shift a week earlier if you can provision sooner.

If you can send a short note on the autoscaling/burst strategy and a ballpark cost delta for reserving 2 additional GPUs for burst we'd appreciate it. Also please send the SOW for signature so procurement can start the internal review.

Appreciate the fast follow-up — looking forward to kicking this off.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme AI
alex.j@acme-ai.com | +1 (650) 555-2100

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme-ai.com>
Date: 2026-02-16T15:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC capacity planning - Acme AI

Thanks Alex — quick technical response on capacity and autoscaling details. Posting here so the plan is explicit and actionable before the kick-off.

Summary of recommended POC capacity plan (based on Acme's profile):
- Baseline reserved: 4 x H100 (dedicated to Acme POC) — supports ~45–60 req/s for 16k context with our standard medium-sized model variant
- Autoscale policy:
  - Scale up trigger: sustained RPS > 90 for 90 seconds or CPU/GPU util > 70% sustained for 60 seconds
  - Scale step size: +2 GPUs per scale event up to a maximum of 8 GPUs (auto-scale window enforced to avoid oscillation)
  - Burst pool: short-lived burst capacity (pre-warmed) up to additional 4 GPUs (total 12) for sub-5-minute spikes — this is billed as burst usage at a different rate and subject to a burst budget
- Hot spares: if Acme wants prepaid spare capacity for guaranteed headroom, we can add 2 reserved hot-spare GPUs that remain idle until needed (recommendation: 2 hot spares for highest reliability)

Fallback & graceful degradation:
- If we hit max capacity and queueing grows, we will route lower-latency requests to a smaller quantized model variant and return a X-Model-Warning header so your application can surface degraded mode.

Estimated cost delta (very rough, final will be in SOW):
- Baseline 4x H100: $XX,XXX / month (pro-rated for POC length)
- Add 2 prepaid hot-spare GPUs: + ~30% on top of baseline for reserved pricing
- Burst usage pricing: metered at peak rates; we estimate a 1–2 day POC with frequent bursts could increase total POC cost ~15–25% depending on burst volume

Attachments: capacity_estimate_acme.xlsx (contains model choices, perf curves, and cost scenarios). I can run a short benchmark on a snapshot of your eval set to refine numbers ahead of the kick-off.

Proposed next steps:
- Alex: confirm whether you'd like prepaid hot-spares (2 GPUs) or rely on burst pool-only.
- Marissa/Dylan: if Alex wants hot-spares we'll add to the SOW and update the cost section; otherwise we'll keep the burst pool approach and call out expected risk profile.
- Schedule 30-min kick-off for Mar 8 — Monica to lead tech runbook.

--
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
